separate_session_evidence: Docs: Codex CLI `exec` is non-interactive, emits JSONL events, and `exec resume <THREAD_ID>` continues a specific recorded thread. Observed (scoped, 2026-09-23): five CLI calls all exited 0; fresh parent and child threads were distinct, the parent exited before the child, and three later resumes used the exact child ID and matched the history marker. See evidence/codex-native-marker-20260923.json. App standalone scheduled tasks start a new chat per run, while in-chat tasks return to that chat; the CLI has no Scheduled management interface.
scheduler_evidence: Documented on the ChatGPT app/web scheduled-tasks surface; app schedules are separate from CLI exec/resume. The reviewed developer-commands source documents /goal and no /schedule entry was found (2026-09-23); this source review and the local in_app_local_automation availability flag do not establish an exec-session scheduler. Scoped observations include a finite external-driver due event and the completed isolated-profile external background-controller proof. Neither establishes a native Codex scheduler or pause/stop of active Codex work; see capability_records and the cited proof artifacts.
lifecycle_evidence: Docs: thread-scoped goals expose set/check/pause/resume/clear; exact-ID CLI resume continues history but does not establish native Codex active-process pause or stop. The earlier finite-driver pause/stop windows suppressed only future dispatches. A separate Linux isolated-profile proof observed external-controller process-group pause/stop, reconciliation, stale-controller recovery, terminal stop, and cleanup; those process controls do not establish OpenForage worker checkpoint/stop semantics. App scheduled tasks are a separate surface.

identity: Session IDs. --session continues a specific session; --fork forks a session when continuing.

separate_session_evidence: Docs: --continue continues the last session, --session <id> continues a specific session ID, and --fork forks the session when continuing; opencode session list enumerates sessions and supports JSON output. The experimental background-subagent flag is not evidence of a separate CLI process and must not be treated as one. Scoped observations in the earlier native marker run and the separate isolated-profile controller proof recorded a fresh parent exiting before a distinct child, followed by continuation to the exact recorded child session; see the individual capability_records and evidence artifacts.
scheduler_evidence: Not documented in the official CLI reference; opencode serve is a server surface, not a scheduler.
